messages:
Avery: Follow-up from the all-hands: a few customers asked for more detail on how we segment the market. Can leadership share a simple framework we can reuse in decks?
Kate (CEO): High-level segmentation: 1) Product-first startups (fast iteration, low friction) -> Hosted. 2) Scale SaaS (predictable traffic, cost sensitivity) -> Dedicated. 3) Regulated/finance/health customers (compliance & isolation) -> Private.
Avery: Helpful. How do we qualify a prospect into one of these quickly on a discovery call?
Jordan: Quick checklist: expected qps, data residency needs, org tolerance for infra work, timeline to production. If qps is variable and timeline is short -> Hosted. If steady high qps or strict SLOs -> Dedicated.
Lina: When customers ask "what does predictable economics mean?" what's the 1line answer?
Kate (CEO): Predictable economics = you can forecast inference spend within a known band and control unit cost via primitives (batching, caching, reserved capacity).
Samir: Practical: can we show a mini-experiment template SEs can run to justify Dedicated? e.g., run hosted for 4 weeks and log 95th p99 token rate?
Jordan: Yes. SE playbook idea: 1) run a 2-4 week POC on Hosted, capture token throughput distribution, tail latency, and peak sustained qps; 2) run Optimize recommendations and measure token cost delta; 3) if projected committed spend surpasses reserved threshold or SLOs fail, propose Dedicated.
Avery: Can we give a short script/command for infra folks to export the measurement metrics?
Samir: Example pseudo-command to pull p99 token rate from analytics: 
```sh
redwood-cli metrics export --start=now-30d --end=now --group=token_rate --percentile=99 --output=csv
```
Lina: Nice. About competitor claims: sales asked whether we can benchmark latency head-to-head in outbound collateral.
Kate (CEO): No public benchmarks without legal and reproducible methodology. Internally, teams can run controlled comparisons as long as methods are documented and reproducible; GTM can convert vetted results into claims via Legal.
Avery: How do we prioritize building features that support those segments? e.g., deeper KMS integrations for Private vs. optimizer tuning for Hosted?
Kate (CEO): Product priority = impact on our mission (production predictability + low friction) and expected customer ARR. If a Private feature unlocks enterprise deals with significant ARR, high priority. Otherwise, pick features that benefit multiple segments first.
GTM-bot: All-hands recording and framing doc uploaded: https://redwood.internal/all-hands/1789012345 :memo:
Avery: Thanks — I'll draft a one-pager (segmentation + quick qualification checklist + SE playbook) and put it in #product-playbooks for review.
